title: Show a population’s age and sex in a pyramid, one bar a year of age.
rule: Draw one thin bar a year of age on each side, men to the left and women to the right on one scale, the youngest at the bottom and ages labeled down the center. Both sides take one ink, and position and the names over each half carry sex. A band of ages the title names takes the view’s red as one job (Rule 14.6) while that red stays within 5 percent of the drawing at every width (Rule 05.1), and the subject ink where it would pass it, as ages 55 to 64 do here. Every other age takes the light fill. Set the band’s words in the empty corner, naming its ages and never its color.
use_when: The reader asks how many people are at or near a given age, such as the ages of retirement programs, or how a population’s ages are shaped.

use_instead.when: The reader compares a few broad age groups
The reader follows one age group’s count over years
Two populations’ age shapes need one picture

text: Single years show the echoes of booms and slumps in births that five-year groups smooth away, and a mirrored scale lets the reader compare men and women at every age by length alone. One ink for both sides keeps color free for the band the story names.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form population-pyramid: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s53; labels.left and labels.right name the two sides, labels.point (red) or labels.named (the subject ink) a range of ages, labels.band_words its words.
